title: Complexity claims
summary: Review a performance claim by reading the loops instead of trusting the comment.

scenario.briefing: A colleague says a duplicate detector runs in linear time. The code is short. Review the loops before accepting the claim.

objectives.description: Choose an appropriate way to validate performance claims.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Count how many times the inner loop runs for each outer iteration.
For every element, the inner loop scans the remaining elements.
That is roughly n × n comparisons, not n.
Reject the linear claim. Measure with growing input sizes and use the growth shape as evidence.

misconceptions.description: Accepting a linear-time comment on a nested loop.
misconceptions.feedback: The code scans the input inside another scan. A comment cannot change the growth rate.
A single timing mixes input size with machine speed and noise. Measure several sizes and compare the trend.

misconceptions.description: Treating a code comment as performance evidence.
misconceptions.feedback: Comments describe intent. Use the algorithm's structure and measurements across input sizes.

sections.title: Complexity is about growth
sections.body: Big-O describes how work grows as input grows, ignoring constant factors. A nested loop over the same input often indicates O(n²). A single pass is O(n). Reading structure gives a model; measurements test that model on real hardware.

sections.title: Measure the right thing
sections.body: Wall-clock time includes noise. Measure several input sizes, use representative data, and look at the shape of growth. A micro-optimization without a measured problem is usually wasted effort.

vocabulary.definition: A loop whose body contains another loop.
A measurement of performance under defined conditions.

steps.title: Review the duplicate detector
steps.prompt: Select every supported finding and choose a verdict.

artifact.title: Duplicate detector
artifact.caption: Submitted with a comment claiming linear time.

findings.label: The function contains nested loops over the values.
The comparison count grows quadratically, not linearly.
The O(n) comment is contradicted by the code.
The function runs in constant time because it returns early sometimes.
A Set could reduce the expected time to O(n).

verdicts.label: Reject the claim and measure or redesign with a Set

steps.explanation: The nested loop is quadratic in the worst case. A Set can track seen values in one pass.
hints: Find the loops that depend on the input size.
Check whether the comment matches the code.
Ask what evidence would confirm the growth rate.
Reject the change: the nested scan is quadratic, and the comment is not evidence.

steps.title: Measure growth
steps.prompt: Which experiment best tests whether a function is linear or quadratic?

options.label: Measure several input sizes and compare how time grows

quiz.explanation: Growth is visible only by comparing multiple sizes. A single timing cannot separate linear from quadratic behavior.

hints: One measurement confounds input size with machine noise.
Several input sizes reveal a growth trend.
A comment describes intent, not runtime.
Choose measure several sizes and compare the growth.

steps.title: Evidence for performance

statements.label: Loop structure informs a complexity estimate.
Measurements should use multiple input sizes.
A comment is sufficient proof of performance.
Optimizing without a measured problem can add complexity for no benefit.

steps.explanation: Estimates guide design; measurements verify behavior under realistic conditions.
hints: Complexity describes how work grows, not one stopwatch reading.
Measurements need more than one input size.
Comments can be stale or wrong.
Select structure, measurement, and avoiding premature optimization; reject comments as proof.
